clue.text: High churchman extends his hand to all corners of the earth

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church
to point is to stretch out a hand or finger towards something

explanation.surface: A senior prelate reaches out in blessing to the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are the four main compass directions, reaching every quarter of the globe.

clue.text: Complaining bitterly by the fence

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling as they lean over the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing is a verb form meaning protesting angrily, and also a barrier of bars, as round a garden.

clue.text: One cleric retiring in Buckinghamshire

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: going backwards, as one retreats, so the word for the cleric is read from right to left

parts.note: Rev is the short form of Reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: A clergyman goes into retirement in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire is an English county west of London; the clue's 'in' makes the definition a place within it, and 'retiring' sends the cleric backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Iver is a village in the south of that county, near Slough.

clue.text: A spirit suitable to be served up before dinner

definitions.text: A spirit suitable to be served up before dinner

parts.note: a peri is a fairy-like spirit of Persian legend

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the word for suitable is written bottom to top

parts.note: fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Advice on a drink fit to offer guests before the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns FIT into TIF in this down light. The whole clue also describes the drink itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-dinner drink, such as sherry, is taken to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Area surrounding a great house

indicators.note: the word for area wraps round the single letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a place is an area or locality

explanation.surface: The grounds that enclose a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts A inside PLACE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the grand residence of a monarch or bishop.

clue.text: Where drinks are served and drunk

explanation.surface: A note on how drinks are poured and then knocked back.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase is the vessels tea or wine goes into; idiomatically it means intoxicated.

clue.text: An annuity can be written in note form

indicators.note: the word for can is set down inside the rearranged letters
to form the word note anew is to rearrange its letters

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A pension plan that may be drawn up in the form of a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb of permission but is the noun, a container; 'form' is the anagram signal on the word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is a shared investment scheme whose payments go to the survivors among the subscribers.

clue.text: Emergency fare for the anaemic

parts.note: military emergency food supplies, read whimsically as a diet for someone short of the mineral that anaemia lacks

explanation.surface: Food kept for a crisis, suitable for the pale and tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers carry such packs of survival food for when normal supplies fail; anaemia is often iron deficiency.

clue.text: Realised movement of the stars

indicators.note: a movement of letters shifts them into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomer grasps how the heavens move.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal describes time or motion measured against the fixed stars, as in astronomy.

clue.text: He has things to confess with hesitation

parts.note: to own up is to confess
er is the sound of hesitating speech

explanation.surface: A man with something to admit hesitates over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is a person who possesses property.

clue.text: Couple competent to frame ordinance, as expected

indicators.note: the pair and competence go round the order as a frame round a picture

parts.note: pr is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
able means competent
an edict is a decree or ordinance

explanation.surface: Two capable officials draft a regulation, just as everyone anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreseeable turns out just as people anticipated it would.

clue.text: Run to assist in police swoop

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
to aid is to assist

explanation.surface: Officers hurry over to help with an arrest operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise visit by officers to search premises or make arrests.

clue.text: Prudence is required in changing doctrine

indicators.note: the little word is needed inside the rearranged letters
the letters of doctrine undergo change into a new order

explanation.surface: Caution is needed when altering established beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a verb in the surface but is fodder kept as written, placed after the first letter of the rearranged doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean careful good judgement about what to say or do.

clue.text: Saint, king, fishermen and murderers

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
anglers fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A list of an odd crew: holy man, monarch, people with rods, and killers.
explanation.definitionFit: Throttlers kill by choking their victims, so they are killers.

clue.text: Type of grass cut down by a docker

explanation.surface: Meadow plants mown by a man from the wharf.
explanation.walkthrough: A docker here is not a port worker but someone who docks, or shortens, animals' tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog's-tail is a meadow grass with spiky seed heads; docking means cutting short a dog's tail.

clue.text: Plan for chemical plant in South Africa

indicators.note: to plant something in is to set it inside, so the short chemical word goes within

parts.note: chem is a short form of chemical

explanation.surface: A scheme to build a chemical works in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagram of a scheme.

clue.text: Depart speedily if the hunt is cancelled

explanation.surface: Advice to leave quickly when the day's sport is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot off is to leave in a hurry; read as 'shoot off' it says the shooting expedition is not happening.

clue.text: Wise man about to have a fight

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
to spar is to fight, as boxers do

explanation.surface: A sage on the verge of a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Caspar is traditionally named as one of the three Magi who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Half hurried back from study class

parts.note: semi is a prefix meaning half

indicators.note: going back means the word for hurried is written in reverse

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A student rushed halfway home from a tutorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small group meeting for discussion and study, as at university.

clue.text: Indian bread and tea set before Italian diva

indicators.note: one piece is placed in front of the other in the answer

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea
Adelina Patti was a celebrated nineteenth-century opera soprano of Italian parentage

explanation.surface: Flatbread and a cuppa served up to an opera star.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is an unleavened flatbread from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Cavalry unit barracked when made to enter together

parts.note: a troop is a cavalry subdivision
soldiers who are barracked are in, housed in their quarters

explanation.surface: Mounted soldiers were jeered when forced to go in as a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barracked' looks like jeered; it means quartered, so IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To troop in is to come in as a group, one after another.

clue.text: He manages daily to ride out and about

indicators.note: letters that are out and about are wandering, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A busy man who likes to go riding round the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every day, and the person in charge of its content runs it.

clue.text: Equip old fellow for the final conflict

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
aged means old
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Kit out an elderly academic for the last battle.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation it is the site of the last great battle between good and evil.

clue.text: Radio comedian is to start broadcasting

explanation.surface: A wireless funnyman is about to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a classic BBC radio comedy series of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A Goon was one of its comic performers, such as Spike Milligan; to go on air is to begin transmitting.

clue.text: Slight legato effect

explanation.surface: A small musical touch that joins notes smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insult, and in music a curved mark telling the player to bind notes together.

clue.text: Liberal Inkatha opponents given oriental weapon

parts.note: the African National Congress was the main rival of the Inkatha movement in South African politics
E for east, the orient

explanation.surface: South African political rivals armed by an Asian supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight.

clue.text: Slovenly female featured by English novelist

indicators.note: the woman is shown first, followed by the letter for English

parts.note: a trollop is an untidy or disreputable woman

explanation.surface: A slatternly woman appears as a character in an English writer's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels in Victorian England.

clue.text: Footnote alluding to an angry remark

parts.note: cross means angry
a reference is a remark mentioning something

explanation.surface: A small note in a book that refers to a bad-tempered comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A note in a text directing the reader to another passage is a kind of footnote.
